# SpeechAudioInput

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Speech.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Speech.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Speech/SpeechAudioInput.cs#L14)

Where [`SpeechRecognitionManager`](/api/vrframework-speech-runtime/SpeechRecognitionManager) gets its audio. A live microphone is the one
that ships; deriving from this is how a scene feeds the recogniser from somewhere else, such
as a recorded clip while testing without a headset on.

The manager polls [`ReadSamples()`](/api/vrframework-speech-runtime/SpeechAudioInput#readsamples) every frame and only while
[`IsCapturing`](/api/vrframework-speech-runtime/SpeechAudioInput#iscapturing) is true, so an input that has nothing to give says so rather
than blocking.

```csharp
public abstract class SpeechAudioInput : MonoBehaviour
```

## Properties

### IsCapturing {#iscapturing}

Whether audio is arriving right now. The manager holds the recogniser idle while this is
false, so silence from a stopped microphone is never mistaken for silence from a quiet room.

